candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record strongly supports leukemia cutis: the patient has pancytopenia (leukopenia, anemia, thrombocytopenia, neutropenia) consistent with an underlying leukemic process, and the biopsy shows a dense dermal infiltrate of monotonous neoplastic cells with dispersed chromatin and high N:C ratio — morphology typical of leukemic blasts rather than lymphomatous cells. Leukemia cutis represents secondary cutaneous involvement by a systemic leukemia, whereas primary cutaneous T-cell lymphoma is a primary skin-based lymphoproliferative disorder without an underlying systemic leukemia. These are distinct diagnostic entities with incompatible scope (primary vs. secondary) and likely different cell lineages.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Primary cutaneous T-cell lymphoma vs. leukemia cutis (secondary cutaneous involvement by leukemia)

case_quality_flags: Underlying leukemia subtype (AML, CLL, etc.) not specified in record but pancytopenia pattern and blast morphology favor acute leukemia
